name: Mattermost Request Hub
description: Request Hub: gated requests for channel creation, Channel Admin, team creation/membership/guests, Team Admin, bots, and webhooks, routed to approvers with two-way messaging.

settings_schema.header:
## Mattermost Request Hub

Governance plugin: non-admins request channel creation, Channel Admin promotion, Team Admin promotion, team creation, team membership, guest invites, bot accounts, and incoming/outgoing webhooks, all via /mattermost-request-hub or the sidebar UI. Requests route to the appropriate approval channel; System Admins (and optionally Team Admins) approve or deny with full two-way messaging.

**Bot and webhook requests use two-step approval**: one security approver and one system approver, identified by the User Attributes configured below.

**Breaking change:** plugin ID changed in 0.5.0. Uninstall the previous Mattermost Request Hub / channel-requests bundle before installing this one (settings and pending KV tickets do not migrate).

### Approval channel routing

The plugin auto-creates these private channels in the approval team on first use:

| Request type | Auto-created channel |
|---|---|
| Channel creation, Channel Admin | Mattermost: Channel Requests (root or per-team) |
| Bot account creation | mattermost-bot-requests |
| Incoming / outgoing webhooks | mattermost-webhook-requests |
| Team creation, Team Admin, team member, guest | mattermost-team-requests |
| Audit log | mattermost-audit-requests |

All channels are seeded with System Admins automatically. Configure the root approval team below, then set up channel domain prefixes.

[View the documentation](/plugins/com.mattermostfederal.mattermost-plugin-request-hub/public/help/docs.html)

settings.help_text: When enabled, users can request the creation of new channels. Turn this off to hide channel-request entry points and reject submissions.
When enabled, members can request Channel Admin promotion on an existing channel.
When enabled, users can request the creation of new teams for admin approval. Also shows a + on the team rail for non–System Admins when native Create Team is hidden.
When enabled, users can request Team Admin promotion on a team they belong to.
When enabled, users can request that existing Mattermost users be added to a team. Routed to mattermost-team-requests for System Admin approval.

When enabled, users can request a guest invite to a team. Email is required. On approval, Mattermost emails a channel-scoped guest invitation (InviteGuestsToTeam), not a regular team signup link. Requires Guest Accounts enabled. Routed to mattermost-team-requests.
When enabled, users can request a bot account (optional token and webhooks). Bot requests require two-step approval (security + system).

When enabled, a bot requester must tick a box accepting the compliance statement below before the request is submitted. The acceptance, its time and the exact text are kept with the request and in its audit history. Agents (MCP) can't submit bot requests while this is on.

The statement bot requesters accept. Leave blank for the built-in statement: the requester won't misuse the bot and is responsible for everything done with it, its tokens and its webhooks. Changing it doesn't change what earlier requesters accepted.
When enabled, users can request incoming or outgoing webhooks. Webhook requests require two-step approval (security + system).

Bot/webhook requests need two distinct people: (1) a security reviewer from the pool below, then (2) a System Admin. Default is User Groups (create the security-approvers group and add reviewers). User Attributes is optional for ABAC/CPA. System Admins only is a setup backup where one System Admin can complete both steps.

Shown when mode is User Attributes. CPA / User Attribute name for the security review. Required: System Admins do not cover this step. Default is security_approver even if that attribute is not created yet.

Shown when mode is User Groups. Mattermost user group whose members must complete the security review (LDAP/plugin-synced, or a custom group when Allow custom approver groups is on). Required: System Admins do not cover this step. Default is security-approvers even if that group is not created yet.

Used when mode is User Groups. On by default so a custom security-approvers group works without LDAP. Anyone who can manage that group's members can make themselves a security approver, so lock down Custom Groups permissions (System Console > User Management > Permissions). Off: only LDAP and plugin-synced groups are used.

When enabled (default), the plugin auto-creates a dedicated approval channel (mattermost-channel-requests) in each team that has at least one Team Admin or System Admin member. Channel and Channel Admin requests from that team route there instead of the primary approval team's root channel. All ticket channels (including Mattermost: Team Requests) are kept in a managed sidebar category named Mattermost: Request Hub.

When enabled, Team Admins of the approval team can approve or deny channel-creation requests in addition to System Admins. Team Admins of the team a channel is requested in can always act on that request. Channel Admin requests are always reviewed by System Admins and the Team Admins of the channel's own team, whatever this is set to. Nobody but a System Admin can approve their own request.

settings.display_name: Approval team's Team Admins can approve team and Team Admin requests
settings.help_text: When enabled, Team Admins of the approval team can approve or deny team creation and Team Admin requests in addition to System Admins, and are added to the Mattermost: Team Requests channel. Warning: they can then make anyone a Team Admin on any team, including teams they don't belong to. That is close to System Admin trust, so turn this on only where System Admins are scarce and you trust those Team Admins fully. Nobody but a System Admin can approve their own request.
Structured editor: define allowed channel prefixes (team-, project-, etc.) with descriptions and suffix rules. Requesters pick from a dropdown; the resulting channel URL is prefix+suffix.

When true, the Mattermost Agents plugin can list prefixes, file requests of every type on a user's behalf and look up pending ones, under the same rules and per-type settings as the request forms. Every request goes to the approvers, including System Admins' requests. Agents can never approve or deny. Takes effect on save; per-tool access is managed in Agents' System Console.
How many requests of each type one user can have waiting for review, up to 1000. Each type is counted separately. 0 means no limit.
Pending requests older than this can no longer be approved, and stop counting toward the per-user limit. At most 3650. 0 means requests never expire. Applies to existing requests too.

How long an access token issued with an approved bot request stays valid. From a month before it expires, the requester gets a weekly reminder, and daily in the last week; System Admins get them if the requester's account is gone. Only affects tokens issued after the change; this is not the request expiry above. Needs Mattermost 11.9 or later: on older servers tokens never expire and no reminders are sent.

How much the plugin posts to the Mattermost: Audit Requests channel. This only changes the channel: every event on every request is always kept in the request history (see /mattermost-request-hub audit and the audit export) and sent to the server audit log, whatever is chosen here.

options.display_name: Every lifecycle event (submissions, approval steps, failures)
Everything, including refusals and every relayed message

settings.help_text: When true, System Admins can download the audit history straight from Audit history in the Request Hub, the audit slash command and the export API. When false (the default), every export is a request: anyone allowed to ask (a security approver, or a System Admin) submits one with a reason, another System Admin approves it, and the file is posted in the requester's request thread. Each export is recorded either way.

Do not enable in production. When true, System Admins can run /mattermost-request-hub exercise populate, teardown and status to seed marked EXERCISE data into a team: persona accounts nobody can sign in as, a channel, and pending requests of every type on the approval cards. Needs channel requests allowed, a channel prefix, and each type the scenario seeds turned on. Approving a seeded request does the real thing (a channel, team, bot or webhook marked EXERCISE, a Team Admin or member change for a persona, or a guest invite to an address that receives no mail). Teardown closes the requests, deletes the webhooks and bots, archives the teams and channels, undoes the personas' team changes and deactivates them. Guest invites can't be withdrawn and expire on their own.

Leave blank to use the built-in fictional scenario. Paste a scenario here to seed your own personas, channels and requests instead. It is stored only in this server's configuration. The format is described in the plugin documentation.
